newsitem.title: USA: Late NYMEX Hub natgas holds modest technical gains.
newsitem.headline: Late NYMEX Hub natgas holds modest technical gains.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures held modest gains late Tuesday in fairly active trade, helped by technical buying and short covering after downside momentum stalled at support early, industry sources said.
At 1440 EDT, June was still up 1.5 cents at $2.23 per million British thermal units, while July was 1.9 cents higher at $2.265. Most others were steady to up by 2.7 cents.

"Locals tried to break June down below $2.18 early but couldn't, then locals and traders covered and ran it back up again," said one Texas trader, adding mild weather forecasts and fund rolling could pressure June before its May 28 expiry.
He said he expected later this week to see funds more aggressively roll length from June into July, adding June could test key support in the $2.05 area before expiration.

Meanwhile, chart traders agreed the market was stuck in a range, with June support and resistance still seen at $2.15 and $2.30, respectively. Major buying was likely at the $2.05 double bottom, with key selling expected at the $2.43 contract high.
The 6-10 day Weather Express forecast is calling for normal to below-normal weather for the eastern two-thirds of the nation, with the West and southern Texas expected above-normal.
Maintenance on Transco's Texas line will continue to cut about 400 mmcfd out of a total capacity of about 600 mmcfd Tuesday through Thursday.

Planned work on Mobil's Mary Ann gas processing plant in Coden, Alabama, has cut the plant's total processing capacity of 380-390 mmcfd. About 120 mmcfd should be back within the next seven days, with the balance due back in three weeks.

In the cash Tuesday, Gulf Coast swing prices slipped a few cents to the high-teens. Midcon pipes were down slightly to about $2.00. New York city gate gas was quoted about five cents lower in the mid-$2.40s.
Early injection estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA storage report ranged from 50 to 75 bcf.
NYMEX said 46,870 contracts traded at 1435 EDT.
On the KCBT, June was still one-half cent higher at $2.07, while deferreds were steady to up 2.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by one cent to 16.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
